messages.subject: SEM without a Measurement Model?
parts:
Dear lavaan Community

I need a quick guidance on the following issue. 

I was running SEM with an all categorical dataset and was facing the positive definite and negative variances problem. 

Therefore as an alternate method I tried to create count variables by adding the relevant indicators and create the count variables in the CSV file itself for each of the construct. 

This way I obtained the count variables and ran it in the structural model with all the covariance and variance calculation. 

I want to ask is it correct to run SEM this way (stating specifically- running SEM without a measurement model)? 

Kindly provide me some direction on this. 

Kind regards
Priya

messages.subject: Re: SEM without a Measurement Model?
parts:
Hi
if i understand your problem and question, I think you have run a path analysis model that is a submodel of SEM. look at this page for more information.

for the positive and negative variances problem, you have to say what the problem is exactly. do you mean heywood case in SEM literature?. if so, have a look at your variables correlations, maybe there are high correlation between your variables and deleting them can resolve the problem. also look to the correlation of latent variables. if it is high, you have to combine your latent variables, of course if it is logical in your research. 
Best
